To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of oscillatory pressuring at elevated temperature (60°C) and high pressure (689MPa) is a promising technology to inactivate B. nivea ascospore in fruit juices.

the inactivation of Byssochyamys nivea ascopores suspended in fruit concentrates by high hydrostatic pressure treatment depends on the water activity of the product, the pressure level, the number of pressure cycles and the temperature.

oscillatory high hydrodynamic pressure treatments are more efficient than continuous high hydrostatic pressure in the inactivation of B. nivea ascospore suspensions in fruit juice concentrates at high temperatures and low aw values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient method to reduce the viability of B. nivea ascospore inocula suspended in juice concentrates, with the objective of extending the shelf‐life of these products.
the development and application of oscillatory pressuring as an alternative to continuous pressure treatments for the inactivation of B. nivea ascospore suspensions in fruit juice concentrates.
the development of new technologies for food preservation, which are able to inactivate microorganisms in fruit juices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of oscillatory pressuring at 689 Pa with five cycles of 1 s at 60 C is an effective method for the inactivation of B. nivea ascospore in both apple and cranberry concentrates.
the use of oscillatory pressuring is not recommended for the inactivation of Byssochyamys nivea ascopores suspended in fruit juices.

the use of oscillatory pressure treatment at elevated temperatures (60 °C) and high water activity (aw) (0·98) is a promising method to inactivate B. nivea ascospore in fruit juice concentrates, and that the application of oscillatory pressure treatments may provide a viable alternative to continuous pressurization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

oscillatory pressure cycles at 60 C can be used as a nonthermal method for inactivation of B. nivea ascospore in juice concentrates, and that the effectiveness of this treatment depends on aw and temperature.
oscillatory pressure treatments are more effective than continuous treatments for inactivating B. nivea ascospore suspensions in fruit juice concentrates, especially at higher temperatures.
oscillatory pressure treatments can be used as a potential non‐thermal preservation method for apple and cranberry juices.

the oscillatory pressure treatments are more effective than continuous pressurization in inactivating B. nivea ascospore populations in fruit juice concentrates.
oscillatory pressurized treatments can be a useful tool for inactivation of B. nivea ascospore inocula in fruit juice concentrates.
